dsv41.label: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
dsv41.description: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017: 552B-parameter mixture-of-experts, 1M-token context, FP8 with FP4 experts, 510 GB. Needs 2 nodes (8 GPUs): the weights alone exceed one node's memory.
notes: Layout is tensor-parallel 4 per node x data-parallel 2 + expert parallel. Pipeline parallel across nodes fails in vLLM 0.33 for this model (AssertionError in _run_layers).
vLLM puts the ~196B-parameter Engram embedding tables in pinned host RAM by itself (about 24 GiB per rank).
Ray is not in the vLLM image, so the run uses vLLM's built-in multi-node data-parallel mode.
The preset's deepseek_v41 reasoning and tool-call parsers fix the stray </think> that the first, parser-less run showed at the start of replies.

glm53.label: GLM-5.3-Flash
glm53.description: zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: MoE with 288 routed experts, 1M-token context, FP8, 328 GB. Needs 2 nodes. Runs with --enforce-eager because CUDA graphs hang on this layout, so these numbers are a floor, not the best this hardware can do.
notes: CUDA-graph capture hung at 12/19 for 22 minutes with no error (DP 2 x TP 4 + EP), so the preset uses --enforce-eager. Open item: find a graph mode that works, or try TP 8 across both nodes as the vLLM recipe does on one 8-GPU node.
First start JIT-compiles FlashInfer kernels and vLLM gives up after 600 s by default: VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 is set in node_entry.sh.
The recipe's glm5_next tokenizer mode needs the Rust frontend, so the tokenizer is left on auto.
caveats: Eager mode only: decode is several times slower than it could be. Fixing that is the main open item.

qwen38.label: Qwen3.8-27B
qwen38.description: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B: dense 27B, bf16, 55.6 GB, 262k context. Fits on a single GPU (51 GiB of weights).
notes: One GPU is enough; for more throughput raise GPUS and DP_PER_NODE together in scripts/models/qwen38.env.
With one GPU the KV cache holds only about 1.9 full-length (262k) contexts.
caveats: With only about 2 full-length contexts of KV cache, long-context use on one GPU is limited.

flint.label: Flint 40B-A2.5B
flint.summary: 39.8B MoE, ~2.5B active, bf16 (base of the JANGH2 quant)
flint.description: RecursiveSI/flint: 39.8B MoE with ~2.5B active parameters, 256 experts, bf16, 79.6 GB, 262k context. This is the unquantised base of OsaurusAI/Flint-40B-A2.5B-JANGH2; that checkpoint is an Apple-Silicon (MLX) format that vLLM cannot load.
notes: OsaurusAI/Flint-40B-A2.5B-JANGH2 will not load: it is an MLX checkpoint with a custom JANGH 2-bit quantisation. The preset serves the BF16 base instead.
vLLM picks the FLASH_ATTN backend by default but the Flint model code asserts FlashInfer: the preset sets --attention-backend FLASHINFER.
The dense-MLP kernel needs (6144 / TP) to be a multiple of 1024, so tensor-parallel must be 1, 2 or 8. TP 4 fails with assert d % bd == 0. The preset uses TP 2 on 2 GPUs.
caveats: This is the BF16 base model, not the JANGH2 2-bit checkpoint. The quantised file's speed and quality on Apple hardware are not measured here.
The preset sets no reasoning or tool parser.

mimo26.label: MiMo-V2.6-Flash
mimo26.description: XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL: MoE with 256 experts, 1M-token context, FP8 compute from mxfp4-stored weights, 178 GB.
notes: Needs vLLM 0.31 or newer for the mxfp4 weights (the image has 0.33).
The vLLM recipe recommends the -MOPD checkpoint over this -RL one, because -RL can get stuck repeating tool calls. The preset runs the -RL checkpoint; that behaviour was not tested.
4 GPUs is the recipe's minimum; 2 GPUs would not hold the 178 GB of weights plus KV cache.
caveats: This is the -RL checkpoint; the recipe recommends -MOPD for agentic use (tool-call repetition not tested here).

qwen38flash.label: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
qwen38flash.description: Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: MoE, 125B total and 6B active parameters plus a 51B n-gram embedding table, 512 experts, bf16, 360 GB. The embedding table is offloaded to host RAM, leaving 61 GiB of weights per GPU.
notes: The n-gram embedding table is offloaded to host RAM by default, so the job needs the host memory of a full 4-GPU allocation.
The recipe says to keep --max-num-seqs 256 (smaller values hit a Mamba-cache capacity error); it is in the preset's extra args and overrides the default of 64.
Plain bf16: no speculative decoding (MTP) and no FP8 KV cache. The vendor recipe's faster settings target B200 GPUs and were not tried on GH200.
caveats: The vendor recipe notes a single 262k-token request was not tested.

gemma31b.label: Gemma 4 31B
gemma31b.description: google/gemma-4-31B: dense 31B, bf16, 62.6 GB, 262k context, Apache-2.0. The weights fit on one GPU, but a full 262k context needs 2.
notes: Ungated, so no Hugging Face token is needed.

google/gemma-4-31B is the pre-trained base checkpoint: it has no chat template, so the chat smoke test returns an error and the benchmark (which does not use the chat API) is what is measured. The instruction-tuned variant is google/gemma-4-31B-it; the architecture and size are the same, so speed should match, but it was not run.

On one GPU vLLM refuses to start at 262,144 context: the weights take 58 GiB, leaving 24.5 GiB, and the KV cache for one 262k sequence needs 33.3 GiB (max context on 1 GPU is about 147k). The preset uses 2 GPUs (tensor-parallel 2).
Uses vLLM's gemma4 reasoning and tool-call parsers.
caveats: Base (pre-trained) checkpoint with no chat template, not the instruction-tuned -it variant.

gemma26b.label: Gemma 4 26B-A4B
gemma26b.description: google/gemma-4-26B-A4B: MoE with 128 experts (8 active, about 4B active parameters), bf16, 51.6 GB, 262k context, Apache-2.0. Fits on a single GPU.
notes: Ungated, so no Hugging Face token is needed.

google/gemma-4-26B-A4B is the pre-trained base checkpoint: it has no chat template, so the chat smoke test returns an error and the benchmark (which does not use the chat API) is what is measured. The instruction-tuned variant is google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it; the architecture and size are the same, so speed should match, but it was not run.
Uses vLLM's gemma4 reasoning and tool-call parsers.
caveats: Base (pre-trained) checkpoint with no chat template, not the instruction-tuned -it variant.

ornith35b.label: Ornith-1.0-35B
ornith35b.summary: MoE, 256 experts (8 active), bf16, reasoning model
ornith35b.description: ornith-ai/Ornith-1.0-35B: MoE with 256 experts (8 active), about 35B parameters, bf16, 70.3 GB, 262k context, MIT. A reasoning model on the Qwen3.5-MoE architecture.
notes: Ungated, so no Hugging Face token is needed. Needs vLLM 0.19.1 or newer (the image has 0.33).
Uses the model card's flags: qwen3 reasoning parser, qwen3_xml tool-call parser, prefix caching.
It is a reasoning model: the 64-token smoke-test reply is all thinking (returned in the reasoning field, empty content), which is expected and does not affect the benchmark.
One GPU is enough: 65.5 GiB of weights leave a KV cache that holds about 3.4 full 262k-token contexts.

minimax31.label: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash
minimax31.summary: Sparse MoE, 128 experts (4 active), mxfp8 + NVFP4 experts
minimax31.description: MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: sparse mixture-of-experts with 128 experts (4 active), 1M-token context, mxfp8 with NVFP4 experts, 252 GB. Runs on one node of 4 GPUs.
notes: Needs vLLM 0.33 or newer (the image has 0.33.0).
--block-size 128 is mandatory for the sparse attention index cache (a mismatch fails with "No common block size").
Hopper has no FP4 tensor cores, so the NVFP4 experts run through the Marlin MoE kernel (--moe-backend marlin).
The vLLM recipe targets 8 x B300 GPUs with NVFP4 KV cache and speculative decoding; none of that is used here.

nemotron35.label: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
nemotron35.description: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL-120B-A12B-BF16: a hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts with 512 experts (about 12B of 120B parameters active), 1M-token context, BF16, 249 GB. A vision-language model; only text is measured here.
notes: The BF16 repo is used, not the NVFP4 one: Hopper has no FP4 tensor cores.
Runs on one node of 4 GPUs (about 58 GiB of weights per GPU).
Uses the model card's parsers (nemotron_v3 reasoning, qwen3_coder tools) and --max-num-seqs 32.
caveats: Vision-language model benchmarked on text only; image and video input are not measured.
